text:
A: Alright! Can you hear me okay?
B: Yes. I can hear you.
A: Sound. I'm Callum, I'm in St Helens, near Liverpool, sort of between Liverpool and Wigan. Depends who you ask, to be fair.
B: Agnieszka. Wakefield.
A: Oh, not far then, over the Pennines. What do you do?
B: Maths teacher. Secondary.
A: Ah, no way. You look like a maths teacher, I mean that nicely! I had a Mrs Kelly who used to stare at me exactly like that when I hadn't done me homework.
B: Had you done it?
A: Never, no. Got a C in the end, so she must've been doing something right.
B: A C is a pass. She did her job. What do you do?
A: I work at the glassworks, on the float line. So erm, basically you've got this massive furnace, and the molten glass comes out and floats on a bath of tin, and it spreads out flat into a ribbon. I'm on the hot end, so I'm watching temperatures, checking the thickness, flagging any defects. It's all shifts, four on, four off, days and nights.
B: Glass floats on tin. I didn't know that.
A: Yeah, it's mad when you first see it. Tin's heavier, so the glass just sits on top, perfectly flat. That's how you get your windows.
B: My husband would have liked that. He was an engineer. He liked anything that is clever and boring at the same time.
A: Clever and boring, that's the job description, to be fair. Most nights it's boring, which is how you want it. Boring means nothing's gone wrong.
B: Same in a classroom. Boring lesson, nobody is throwing chairs. Good day.
A: Ha! Do they throw chairs?
B: Year 8 on a Friday, everything is possible.
A: Did you do the puzzle bit at the start? I was dead pleased with meself, then I got to the last one and just guessed.
B: I did it. One question had two correct answers. Badly written.
A: Did it? Which one?
B: The one with the shapes, number three. "Choose the best answer." Two were equally good.
A: See, that's why you'd want her on your quiz team. I run a pub quiz team on Thursdays, I'm captain. We could do with someone who argues with the quizmaster.
B: I would argue with the quizmaster. Often he is wrong.
A: He is wrong! Last week he had the Moon landing as '68. Sixty-nine, mate. I've listened to about four podcasts on it.
B: Then you were right. Did you get the point?
A: No! He wouldn't give it me. Still not over it.
B: This is why I do sudoku. Nobody can tell you the answer is wrong when it is right.
A: That's fair, that. Erm, what do you do when you're not marking? Are you from Wakefield originally, or...?
B: Poland. Tarnów. I came 2006. My son is seventeen, A-levels, he eats everything in the fridge. That is my hobby now, buying food for him.
A: Ha, me mum says the exact same about me brother. Is he going uni then?
B: He wants to. Engineering, maybe. Like his father.
A: Ah, that's nice, that. Honestly I sometimes wish I'd gone. I did an apprenticeship instead, and I've no regrets, like, but I do love learning stuff. I've been looking at the company paying for an HNC, in manufacturing engineering.
B: Then do it. If they pay, do it. You will regret it if you don't.
A: Yeah. Yeah, me wife says that too.
B: Then she is also right. Two people telling you.
A: [laughs] Okay, okay, I'll look at the forms on—
